observation: Rare-incident recall collapses although mean validation F1 changes by only 0.03.
A rise in disagreement between independently adapted robots precedes the first labeled failure by 9 to 17 hours.
Uncertainty spikes recur at the same loading zones and shift changes even after the originating robot leaves.
A four-month-old adapter recovers performance in 140 examples; retraining from the current model needs 1,900 examples.
Pairs of intentionally diverse specialists make complementary errors; forcing convergence removes most of the gain.
A 2.2 KB quantile sketch identifies the affected feature stages with 87 percent precision without transmitting images.
Full replay exceeds the adaptation power ceiling and overwrites a specialist that was useful at dusk.
Globally calibrated confidence hides a small but coherent failure cluster at two sites.
A 160-byte site/time bulletin lets later robots increase scrutiny before entering the affected aisle.
The aggregate forgetting score treats rapid recovery of recurrent regimes as failure and masks slow adaptation to truly novel regimes.
Self-training amplifies correlated false positives when every robot begins from the same global checkpoint.
Querying a peer selected by error signature outperforms querying the most similar site by 11 recall points.
Resetting on a calendar boundary destroys gradual adaptation while leaving the causal camera condition unchanged.
Compressed gradients nearly exhaust the daily link budget and reveal less about which failure relation changed than a 3 KB error signature.
Robots can exchange short signed messages peer-to-peer but cannot wait for a fleet-wide barrier during the shift.
A selective second pass stays inside the alert deadline when used on fewer than six percent of frames.
